:::{#thm-law-conditional-prob}
#### Law of conditional probability (probability chain rule, general product rule)

The **law of conditional probability** is also called the **probability chain rule**
or the **general product rule**.
It states that for any two events $A$ and $B$ with $\Pr(B) > 0$:

$$\Pr(A \cap B) = \Pr(A \mid B) \cd \Pr(B)$$

:::

::: proof

Rearranging @def-conditional-prob:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A \mid B) &= \frac{\Pr(A \cap B)}{\Pr(B)} && \text{(definition of conditional probability)}
\\ \Pr(A \cap B) &= \Pr(A \mid B) \cd \Pr(B) && \text{(multiply both sides by } \Pr(B) \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::
